assessment: This important work demonstrates that the transfer of dysfunctional mitochondria stimulates proliferation in recipient cancer cells by serving as a signal to induce reactive oxygen species production that in turn activates signaling pathways that control cell cycle. Compelling cell biology assays including rigorous microscopy with elegant reporters track the function and fate of transferred mitochondria in recipient cells. The work is relevant to the study of mitochondria, cancer, and immune cells and will be of broad interest to cell biologists and biochemists.
